text:
alex: kicking off an apples-to-apples comparison: KV cache pre-warm vs adaptive batching. goal: same replay trace, same model bits, measure p50/p95, tokens/s, and KV hit-rate. summary below.

tara: nice — which harness and exact flags?

alex: here are the two runs i ran back-to-back on the same dedicated pool (4xA100):
```\n# static warmup (preload KV for popular prefixes)\n./harness replay --trace traces/replay-mar10.json --model redwood-v1-13b-q4_0 --kv-warmup=true --adaptive-batching=false --batch-max=32 --ramp=30\n\n# adaptive batching (no prewarm, batch grows with queue)\n./harness replay --trace traces/replay-mar10.json --model redwood-v1-13b-q4_0 --kv-warmup=false --adaptive-batching=true --batch-max=64 --min-latency-ms=15 --aggressive_decay=0.7\n```

smita: how are you computing KV hit-rate in the logs?

alex: we instrumented kernel layer to emit per-request kv_hits / kv_lookups. aggregated report:
```\nstatic_warmup: kv_hit_rate=78% (seq<=512), tokens/s=12.1k, p50=18ms, p95=72ms\nadaptive_batching: kv_hit_rate=41% (cold tails), tokens/s=15.6k, p50=16ms, p95=84ms\n```
notes: adaptive delivered ~29% higher throughput but increased p95 on long sequences by 12ms on average.

ryan: that p95 regression is worrying. where's the extra tail coming from? batching overhead? kv cache misses?

alex: digging into flame graphs: tails are from "kv_lookup_sync" + "cpu-mem-copy" spikes when batch size jumps. Basically adaptive sometimes enlarges batches mid-request, forcing extra KV lookups that miss and block the kernel.

jun: were kernels switching (cuda kernel selection) when batch size changes? that can add a CPU-side selection cost if we didn't cache kernel handles.

alex: good call — we do dynamic kernel selection, and selection cost showed up as ~3-5ms on the worst cases. i tried memoizing kernel choices per batch shape and that shaved ~3ms off p95.

smita: what about quantization tradeoffs? did you try q2/q3 vs q4_0?

alex: quick matrix: all runs on same trace with adaptive batching enabled unless noted.
```\nq4_0 + adaptive: p95=84ms, tokens/s=15.6k, cost_index=1.0, rv_quality=baseline\nq3a + adaptive: p95=90ms, tokens/s=17.0k, cost_index=0.83, rv_quality=-0.7%\nq2 + adaptive: p95=96ms, tokens/s=20.1k, cost_index=0.65, rv_quality=-2.1%\nq4_0 + static_warmup: p95=72ms, tokens/s=12.1k, cost_index=1.25, rv_quality=baseline\n```\ncost_index is normalized per-token compute cost; rv_quality is relative quality measured on our prompt eval set. q3a gives decent cost wins with small quality hit but slightly worse p95. q2 is cheaper but amplifies the p95 tail (likely due to extra CPU quant dequant overhead in critical path).

tara: can we tune the adaptive policy to preserve KV locality? e.g., prefer batching requests with same prefix / key fingerprint?

alex: experimented with a locality-aware bucketer that groups requests by prefix hash before forming batches. results: tokens/s down ~4% vs plain adaptive but p95 improves by ~6-8ms and kv_hit_rate rises to ~60%.

ryan: that's promising. tradeoffs: a small throughput hit for much better tail. might be acceptable for latency-sensitive customers.

smita: any regression gate alerts? we should block rollouts if p95 increases >5ms on canary.

alex: on canary we saw p95 increase of 9ms vs prod baseline when using plain adaptive. i opened PR w/ a feature flag to enable locality-aware adaptive + kernel memoization by default and fall back to static warmup for top 10% latency-critical routes.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: pushed alex/kv-adaptive-tuning 0a1b2c -> staging, running E2E loadtests.

jun: next steps i propose:
- run longer-duration replay (24h) with mixed q-profile to see accumulation effects on KV warmup
- add per-batch kernel-handle cache in runtime (low-risk)
- implement locality bucketer as a tunable policy (turn on for latency SLO routes)
- update regression gate to evaluate both throughput and tail for canaries

alex: agreed. i'll add reproducible configs to the harness and a small doc with the perf matrix. attaching short log excerpt here (snip):
```\n[2026-03-12T14:02:13Z] run=adaptive batch=28 kv_hits=11/42 p95=82ms cpu_kernel_select=4.1ms\n[2026-03-12T14:02:14Z] run=adaptive_locality batch=16 kv_hits=26/39 p95=74ms cpu_kernel_select=0.6ms\n```

tara: thanks — can you drop the harness commands + config to the eng-runtime wiki and tag me? i'll prioritize the canary gate change. :thumbsup:

alex: will do. thanks all.
